messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT /pager -> model-serving-latency detected: P50 latency spike > 600ms for model-prod-1, paging primary oncall (maya r.)

oncall-bot: Escalation policy: 5m ack window, then notify deputy and #eng-oncall. Runbook: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/model-serving-latency

maya r.: i got the pager but i'm stuck getting through airport security. phone on do-not-disturb for next ~40m. can someone pick this up? sorry folks :(

sam (oncall): i can take it. jumping in now — @maya r. any known deployments or config changes in last 30m?

maya r.: nothing on deploys. last config tweak was autoscale tuning 3h ago. logs show KV cache misses ramping. possible origin: cache eviction + batch size spike.

liam: FYI i'm on call shadow but not primary. happy to help with traces if you need. where's the bridge?

anya: pinging infra because we saw a single worker OOM and restart earlier, might correlate. infra ticket #INC-8942.

sam (oncall): creating a bridge. ops-bot: create-bridge model-latency-bridge -> link

ops-bot: Bridge created: https://meet.redwood/bridges/model-latency-1749999999 (open for primary/deputy)

sam (oncall): quick triage plan: 1) confirm customer impact 2) short-term mitigation (route traffic to model-prod-2 / reduce max-batch) 3) investigate root cause (KV cache, worker memory)

liam: checking customer-facing errors now. logs show ~0.8% 5xx spikes for last 3 mins, concentrated in eu-west-1.

maya r.: customers likely seeing latency timeouts at 10s for streaming endpoints. can we reduce request timeout client-side? not in control here — need routing fix. :grimacing:

sam (oncall): ok temporary routing — switch 20% of traffic from model-prod-1 to model-prod-2 and lower max_batch_size to 8 for prod-1. doing that via runtime route override. applying...

sam (oncall): command: ```
# runtimectl route override
runtimectl set-route --model model-prod-1 --weight 80
runtimectl set-route --model model-prod-2 --weight 20
runtimectl config update --model model-prod-1 --max-batch-size 8
```

sam (oncall): applied. monitoring metrics. please watch p50/p95.

liam: p50 dropped from 750ms -> 340ms within 60s. 5xx rate down to 0.2%. looks promising.

anya: infra confirms the worker that OOM'd is on host gpu-12-eu. they're reprovisioning more headroom and checking driver logs.

maya r.: thanks team. i'm going to mark myself as limited for 40m in case anything else pops. leaving handoff notes: primary still me but sam is acting primary for this incident until i'm back. runbook section followed: "if KV cache misses spike, reduce max_batch_size and route traffic to warm replicas".

sam (oncall): noted. i've taken incident lead. can someone add a short blameless note in the incident doc with timeline? i'll start: https://incidents.redwood/1749999999

liam: adding traces and log snippets to the incident page. also adding grafana panel links.

anya: infra will follow up with host remediation + kernel logs; tagging security if anything suspicious. so far looks like memory-pressure regression after a driver bump 6h ago.

maya r.: thanks. one more ask — can we roster a backup for the next 2 hours in case i remain offline? need a deputy to be reachable.

sam (oncall): i'll be reachable and will stay primary until maya confirms back. liam, can you be deputy for 2h?

liam: yep, deputy for next 2h. will hold pager.

anya: i'll monitor infra channel and ping here if host-level remediation needs rolling restart.

oncall-bot: NOTE: maya r. set status "travelling - limited" for 40m. Pager delegation: sam (oncall) acting primary, liam deputy.

sam (oncall): closing loop: customer impact reduced, remediation steps in progress, bridge stays open until incident doc marked stable. next steps for postmortem: confirm root cause (driver bump + cache pressure), consider auto-fallback policy to spawn warm replicas in EU region, add canary for driver upgrades.

maya r.: back online, phone on. thanks everyone for covering — huge help. i'm on bridge now.

liam: all good from traces side. i'll stay on call until handoff at +2h.

sam (oncall): thanks all. logging final timeline and moving incident to monitoring state. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Pager resolved for model-serving-latency. Incident status -> monitoring."
